verdict.rationale: Meilisearch documents a native, first-party MCP server at POST /mcp. Its docs say users can create indexes, add documents, configure settings, tune ranking rules and run searches "using natural language prompts" from an MCP-compatible AI client, so the product can be operated conversationally. Missing for 10: no hands-on or independent corroboration of the natural-language operation, no documented coverage limits for which admin operations work this way, and it depends on an external AI client rather than a built-in natural-language console.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Once configured, you can create indexes, add documents, configure settings, and perform searches using natural language prompts.
Update ranking rules, searchable attributes, and faceting through natural-language prompts.
Index documents, tune ranking rules, and search Meilisearch through natural conversation in the AI client you already use.
Meilisearch ships a native MCP server at the POST /mcp route so any MCP-compatible client can search your indexes directly.
